## GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH
ABSTRACT

Prohibition and Excise – Removal of ARET levied additionally on Bars – Increase of MRPs
by Rs 10/- per bottle across all sizes except certain segments with marginal
augmentation of retailer margin by 1% of MRP - Revision of rates of Additional Retail
Excise Tax on Indian Made Foreign Liquor, Foreign Liquor, Beer, Wine and RTDs –
Amendment - Notification - Issued.

REVENUE (EXCISE-II) DEPARTMENT

G.O.Ms.No.23

Dated:12-01-2026

## ORDER

Government have reviewed the Excise policies implemented during the period
2019-24 and prepared the Way Forward regarding the Excise policies to be pursued for
the ensuing Excise years. Pursuant to the Way Forward, a Group of Ministers has been
constituted vide GO Rt. No 582, Revenue (Excise) Department, Dt. 29-08-2024, for
recommending draft new comprehensive Excise policy on retail trade, pricing of liquor
and taxation and also vide GO Rt. No. 939, Revenue (Excise-II) Department, dated 28-
08-2025 to examine and provide recommendations to the Council of Ministers on all future
Excise Policy proposals. The GoM has met from time to time and made recommendations
accordingly.

1. In the reference 1ˢᵗ read above, the Government have issued new Excise Policy
2. with respect to Shops for 2024-26 duly fixing number of Shops, method of disposal, Retail
3. Excise Tax (RET), Retailer’s Margin, etc. As per the orders issued in the reference 2ⁿᵈ read
4. above, the Retailer Margin shall be 20% on the Issue price of IMFL, FL, Beer, Wine and
5. Ready to Drink Varieties.
7. In the reference 4ᵗʰ read above, Government have rationalized the Additional Retail
8. Excise Tax (ARET) on IMFL, FL, Beer, Wine and Ready to Drink varieties supplied to the
9. licensees of Shops, Bars and In-Houses.
11. In the reference 5ᵗʰ read above, Government revised the rates and structure of
12. Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET-1 and ARET-2) on Indian Made Foreign Liquor, Foreign
13. Liquor and Beer with a view to ensuring stability of prices and sustainability of retail liquor
14. trade.
16. The Group of Ministers met on 22.12.2025 and discussed, among other things, the
17. effects of levy of ARET additionally on liquor products purchased by Bars.
19. The GoM has noted that before November 2019, the invoice price of IMFL and FL
20. supplied by APSBCL wholesale depots was uniform for both Bars and Retail Shops,
21. ensuring parity in the supply and taxation structure. However, from November 2019,
22. Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET) was additionally levied for the exclusively on IMFL and
23. FL stocks supplied to the bars. This resulted in higher invoice prices for Bars compared
24. to Retail Shops for the same IMFL and FL stocks. Since then, Bars have been paying ARET
25. additionally.

1

1. The exclusive levy of Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET) on liquor supplied to Bars 2. since November 2019 has created a pricing anomaly, with Bars paying higher invoice 3. prices than Retail Shops for identical products supplied from APSBCL depots. This 4. differential treatment is inconsistent with the principle of uniformity in taxation and has 5. led to market distortions. Rationalization of Bar ARET to restore parity between Bars and 6. Shops and eliminate inconsistencies in taxation structure and to promote fairness, 7. transparency, and legal defensibility. 9. Further, to safeguard State revenues, the GoM has recommended a calibrated 10. upward revision of MRPs by Rs 10/- per bottle across all sizes, except in respect of IMFL 11. with MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and RTDs, through revision of existing ARET slabs 12. with a marginal augmentation of retailer margin on IMFL and FL (including IMFL with MRP 13. Rs 99 (180ml), Beer, wine & RTDs) by around 1% of MRP to maintain equity and stability 14. across both the A4 Shop and Bar licensees, while ensuring commercial balance. This 15. calibrated measure will offset the fiscal impact of ARET withdrawal, ensure price parity 16. between trade segments and enhance overall revenue to the State exchequer. 18. In the references 6ᵗʰ and 7ᵗʰ read above, the Director, Excise & Prohibition 19. submitted proposals for removal of the ARET additionally levied on the stocks of IMFL & 20. FL purchased by Bars, while increasing the MRPs of IMFL & FL by Rs 10/- per bottle across 21. all sizes, except in respect of IMFL with MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and RTDs, through 22. structural changes in the ARET slabs along with a marginal augmentation of retailer 23. margin on IMFL and FL (including IMFL with MRP Rs 99 (180ml), Beer, wine & RTDs) by 24. around 1% of MRP. 26. The Government have approved the recommendations of the GoM and issued 27. orders in the reference 8ᵗʰ read above, to remove the Additional Retail Excise Tax 28. additionally levied on Bars and to revise the MRPs of IMFL & FL upwardly by Rs 10/- per 29. bottle across all sizes, except in respect of IMFL with MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and 30. RTDs, through structural changes in the ARET slabs along with a marginal augmentation 31. of retailer margin by around 1% of MRP across the spectrum of IMFL & FL. 33. As directed in the reference 8ᵗʰ read above, the Managing Director, APSBCL has 34. submitted proposals in the reference 9ᵗʰ read above, revising the slabs and rates of ARET- 35. 1 and 2 in respect of IMFL, FL (Spirits, Beer, Wine, RTD), Beer, Wine and RTD to implement 36. the orders of the Government. 38. The Government after careful examination of the proposal submitted by the 39. Managing Director, APSBCL have decided to revise the slabs and rates of ARET-1 and 2 in 40. respect of IMFL, FL (Spirits, Beer, Wine, RTD), Beer, Wine and RTD. Accordingly, the 41. following Notification shall be published in an extraordinary issue of the Andhra Pradesh 42.
